scope: Opt-in native roster-based fusion selection; not full controller migration or performance acceptance
implementation: OPENMUA2_FUSION_BUTTONS=1 installs guarded observers at two native picker boundaries plus the existing input observer. All remain OFF by default.
Title identity and live code digests are checked; selection resolves ordered live roster handles with native types, controller ownership and input-object identity.
The selected actor replaces only the picker candidate. Original instructions continue, including native actor eligibility, resource and fusion/revival processing.
A/B/X/Y request ordered roster slots0/1/2/3. Self and other human actors are rejected. No cached host selection survives save reload.
Input marker and power/navigation action bits are consumed while LT requests selection; current scalar samples remain available to the picker.
Runtime start-observer registration now supports up to8 unique addresses, dispatched by actual PC and retained across reload.

test_fixture.description: Process-local test device; this is not the default profile. Manual right-stick aiming still confirms the existing tutorial dialog, then partner selection uses LT+face with no pointer offset.

failures_preserved: Initial live B attempt suppressed tutorial confirmation because the LT marker was present during manual aim. No partner selected. Original run remains private under fusion-buttons-b-20261001. Corrected the disposable profile to keep manual confirmation separate.

Read-only caller profiling changed the reference route result and collected no requested entry samples; it is not selection/FPS acceptance. Actual resident-block records located the native picker path.
Initial implementation treated inactive signed direction -1 as invalid. Inspected real scalar data, corrected the selector and added signed-direction tests before successful gameplay probes.
limitations: Three distinct native partner selections and return to idle are numeric behavioral evidence, not inspected animations/effects or audible output.
Self-selection rejected in the prepared team. Other team orders, dead/absent heroes, revival and multiplayer remain unverified.
Release-to-cancel and modal/menu behavior are unfinished; the full MUA1-style layout and exact profile migration remain pending.
The experimental flag requires the matching marker profile. Default v4/custom profiles are not automatically migrated.
No new FPS or audio-quality claim. First successful B run overlapped final build linking, so it is not performance evidence.
